overview: Costa Rica is a small country in Central America, between Nicaragua and Panama. Its capital and largest city is San José. Costa Rica abolished its army in 1948 and is known for being peaceful and stable. It protects a large share of its land in national parks and reserves, and nature tourism is a big part of its economy.

geography.text: Costa Rica has coastlines on both the Caribbean Sea and the Pacific Ocean. A chain of mountains and volcanoes runs down the middle of the country, and the Central Valley among them is where most people live. Rainforests, cloud forests and beaches make it one of the most biodiverse places in the world for its size.

history.text: Costa Rica was a quiet corner of Spain's Central American empire. It became independent in 1821 and grew coffee, and later bananas, for export. After a short civil war in 1948 it abolished its army, and it has been one of Latin America's most stable democracies ever since.

events.title: Independence
events.text: Costa Rica becomes independent from Spain.

events.title: Army abolished
events.text: After a brief civil war, the country abolishes its army.

events.title: Nobel Peace Prize
events.text: President Óscar Arias wins the prize for his peace plan for Central America.

government.text: Costa Rica is a presidential republic. The President is elected every four years and cannot serve two terms in a row. It abolished its army in 1948 and has been one of Latin America's most stable democracies ever since. Its single-chamber Legislative Assembly has 57 members.

economy.text: Costa Rica's economy is built on tourism, medical devices, coffee, bananas and pineapples; it is one of the world's biggest pineapple exporters. Almost all of its electricity comes from renewable sources such as hydropower and geothermal energy.

culture.text: Costa Ricans call themselves 'Ticos' and use the phrase 'pura vida', meaning 'pure life', as a greeting and a way of life. About a quarter of the country is protected as national parks and reserves. Painted ox carts are a national symbol listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Pura vida
items.text: Used to say hello, goodbye, thank you and 'all good'.

items.title: Painted ox carts
items.text: Brightly decorated carts once used to carry coffee.

items.title: Monteverde
items.text: A cloud forest full of orchids and hummingbirds.

sport.text: Football is the most popular sport. Costa Rica surprised the world at the 2014 World Cup by topping a group with Uruguay, Italy and England and reaching the quarter-finals. Surfing is also popular on its Pacific coast.

items.text: Reached the World Cup quarter-finals for the first time.

items.title: Keylor Navas
items.text: Goalkeeper who won three Champions Leagues with Real Madrid.
